segments.he: סיפרו לפני הר' נחמן מטולטשין ז"ל על אחד מגדולי אנ"ש שהוא עושה קידוש ביום שבת קודש בבקר על יין שרף. ולא יישר בעיניו ואמר שהוא אינו אוחז בזה ממה נפשך או אינו יוצא בקידוש או משכר את עצמו. אם הוא שותה כוס קטן אינו יוצא בקידוש כראוי ואם הוא שותה כוס גדול הלא הוא משכר את עצמו כי רבינו ז"ל אמר "בראנפין אביסעל".
segments.en: I heard from our fellowship: when the conscription decrees were issued, everyone was in an uproar and Rabbainu occupied himself greatly with this matter and said several Torah teachings about it, as cited in Chayay Moharan. And Rabbainu said the Torah of chapter ten, Ve'eileh HaMishpatim — that the counsel against this is dancing and clapping of the hands, which sweetens harsh judgments. And then the holy Gaon Reb Dovid Tzvi — the father-in-law of Moharan'as — asked Moharan'as what the Rebbe said should be done about the conscription. [He was the chief rabbi over all the provinces and had decreed multiplied supplications as was customary.] Moharan'as replied that Rabbainu says the counsel is dancing and clapping of hands. He answered: "This also pleases me!" "Gam li yishar be'einay — mir gefelt oykh azoy!" And he commanded his people to do dancing too. The tears and weeping that came from the dancing cannot be described. And plainly: with supplications alone people are liable to fall into sadness — and sadness strengthens all harsh judgments. Therefore when one inclines toward sadness, the judgments intensify further, G-d forbid. The counsel is to break the sadness through dancing — and thereby the harsh judgment that comes through sadness is broken and sweetened — aside from the great secrets in all of Rabbainu's words.
